revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule permits fixed-size unpacked arrays or unpacked structures with recursively valid element types, but does not include unpacked unions in that permitted category.
The 2012 text additionally requires constructor arguments for a const class handle declaration to be constant expressions; the 2023 expectation omits that restriction.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no Clause 6.20.7 rule defining and restricting the context-dependent $ special constant.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits $ syntactically in an open_value_range but does not state the general less-than-or-equal/greater-than-or-equal semantics now guaranteed by Clause 6.20.7.
IEEE 1800-2017 restricts the contexts in which the $ primary is legal but does not impose the 2023 rule that $ must be an entire self-contained expression outside a queue select.
IEEE 1800-2017 treats $ as a value assignable to integer parameters and does not state the 2023 prohibition on direct numeric evaluation such as equality with zero.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits $ for parameters of integer types and restricts use to literal-$ contexts; it does not state the 2023 simple-bit-vector target rule or the explicit queue-context exception.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits $ for parameters of integer types and limits their use to literal-$ contexts, but does not specify the 2023 simple-bit-vector formulation or queue-context exception.

IEEE 1800-2012 specifies success/failure return values, destination preservation, and no run-time error for function-form $cast, but does not provide the 2023 guarantee that it never issues a compile-time error.
IEEE 1800-2017 limits $cast arguments to singulars and permits compile-time checking of singularity; its no-error function behavior applies only after that restriction is met.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires compile-time checking that both arguments are singular, unlike the 2023 statement that no compiler type checking is done.
IEEE 1800-2017 declares both forms with singular destination and source arguments; 2023 extends the signature and behavior to nonsingular data.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits $cast only for singular arguments and has no assignment-compatible nonsingular branch.

IEEE 1800-2012 specifies replication for a single Str operand, converting when Str is string-typed or the multiplier is nonconstant; it does not state the 2023 rule for mixed multioperand inner string concatenations.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits class-scope selection through these incomplete prefixes only in a typedef declaration; 2023 additionally permits the type operator and type-parameter assignments.
IEEE 1800-2012's default-variable table lists class handles as null but does not identify interface-class handles or otherwise provide this explicit default guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines $isunbounded with a constant_expression argument rather than limiting its signature to parameter or hierarchical-parameter identifiers.
IEEE 1800-2017 accepts a constant_expression argument, whereas 2023 restricts the signature to a parameter identifier or hierarchical parameter identifier.

IEEE 1800-2012 states the constant-multiplier rule for replication of a single Str string literal, not the 2023 generalized rule for an inner concatenation containing multiple all-literal Stri operands.
IEEE 1800-2012 parameter-port grammar supports value, local, data-type-led, and type parameter declarations, but its type parameter productions do not include the 2023 optional forward_type category.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines string replication with one inner Str operand; it does not provide the 2023 generalized one-or-more Stri operand form, though its multiplier restrictions otherwise correspond.
IEEE 1800-2012 type parameters cannot include an enum, struct, union, class, or interface-class category constraint.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no type-parameter syntax for constraining an override to enum, struct, union, class, or interface class.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define the restricted class-scope-selection rule for a type-parameter prefix.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits class-scope selection through a type-parameter prefix only in a typedef declaration; 2023 also permits type operators and type-parameter assignments.

IEEE 1800-2012 type-parameter grammar has type followed by type assignments, but does not permit an optional enum/struct/union/class/interface-class forward category or the 2023 incomplete class-scoped assigned-type form.
IEEE 1800-2017 supports type-parameter assignment lists but does not include the optional forward enum/struct/union/class/interface-class category in type_parameter_declaration.
IEEE 1800-2012 Clause 6.23 has no type(this) rule denoting the enclosing class.

IEEE 1800-2012 sends a literal operand with a constant multiplier through numeric-replication semantics and does not guarantee that a zero multiplier always yields string-typed empty string; it gives string N-copy semantics only when the multiplier is nonconstant or the operand is string-typed.
